intro: School principals and district leaders already make high-stakes decisions and manage large staffs. The closest of the 25 careers below is Training and Development Managers, with an 86% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $133,000, which is 26% more than the $105,870 that school administrators from kindergarten through high school earn.
why_it_works: Running a school means hiring and coaching staff, handling parents and budgets, and making calls that affect hundreds of students. O*NET rates judgment and decision making at 4.75 out of 5 for this job, one of the highest scores on the site. Corporate training, human resources and executive roles use that same mix. Every match needs no new degree; the gaps are finance and operations.
tips: Rename school work for business readers: staff development becomes talent development, and school improvement becomes change management.
Human Resources Managers are a 79% match and earn $149,280, which is 41% more.
Take a corporate finance or budgeting course; managing financial resources is a common gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former school administrators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Training and Development Managers (86%), Instructional Coordinators (83%) and Human Resources Managers (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Instructional Coordinators earn $77,440, which is 27% less than the school administrator median, but keep you close to schools.

faq.q: Which careers for school administrators pay more?
faq.a: 12 of the 25 matches pay more than $105,870. Chief Executives earn $213,990 (102% more), Industrial-Organizational Psychologists $193,950 (83% more) and Marketing Managers $166,790 (58% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Psychologist roles usually need specific graduate training.

faq.q: Do school administrators need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than school administrators already have. A master's degree is common, held by 60% of workers in a close match, so most moves depend on your leadership record and how you present it to employers outside education.

faq.q: What skills should school administrators learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operation and control, programming, operations analysis and managing financial resources. Managing people already rates 4.12 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so business and technology skills are the main gap.
